newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB 3.6% bond due March 2000 traded at 8.04%.
newsitem.headline: NCB 3.6% bond due March 2000 traded at 8.04%.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank's 3.6 percent five-year bank debentures due March 2000 were traded at 8.04 percent on Thursday, traders said.
The traded amount was 200 million yen.
Traders also said NCB's five-year debenture with a coupon rate of 3.05 percent due in May 2001 was traded at 7.5 percent.

The market seems to be taking a positive view of NCB's announcement on Thursday that it and Bankers Trust New York Corp had agreed on a business alliance and that NCB would also consider a capital tie-up with the U.S. bank, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Trades in NCB debentures with more than two years left until maturity had been pretty rare until this morning, a trader for a brokerage house said.
The trader said, however, that the basic trend of the market remained unchanged so far.

NCB debentures with a year or less to go until maturity have yields of around six percent, while those with two years or more until maturity are still stuck with yields of seven percent and above, he said.
Traders said NCB's one-year debentures with a coupon rate of 0.8 percent due to mature in October 1997 were traded at six percent this morning.
